subject: Unexpected p99 surge impacting Shopline checkout — ops coordination & customer note
messages:
From: Ayla Choi <ayla.choi@shopline.com>
To: support@redwood.com
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Checkout p99 spike and conversion hit

Hi team,

We started seeing a sharp increase in latency around 08:00 PST for our checkout /v1/generate endpoint. p95 is fine (~200ms) but p99 jumped to ~6s and sessions are timing out — our checkout conversions dropped ~8% in the last 30 minutes.

Attached is a dashboard screenshot and a small slice of our client-side logs. Our retry logic is causing extra load so we want to coordinate closely with you on mitigations.

High-level ask: can Redwood confirm whether this is a customer-wide routing change or an internal degradation? We’re currently risk-averse to falling back to lower-quality variants without understanding impact.

Attachments: service-ops-dash.png (png), canary-logs-0506.tar.gz (log bundle, 6MB)

Thanks,
Ayla Choi
Head of Platform Reliability, Shopline
ayla.choi@shopline.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 09:05:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Checkout p99 spike and conversion hit / action needed

Thanks Ayla — we’re on it.

Internal TL;DR: customer Shopline reporting p99 ~6s on gen endpoint and client-side retries increasing upstream load. Initial bridge created: https://redwood.airplane.dev/bridge/INC-20280605 (owner: karthik).

Immediate asks (please ack and own):
- @karthik_iyer: triage root cause + attach fresh canary logs (include kv-cache miss rates by host and autoscaler churn logs). Priority: 30m.
- @ben_carter: check kernel scheduling/throttles and any recent autoscaler config changes in us-west-2 (any recent rollout?).
- @marissa_cole: product tradeoff — prepare short customer-safe mitigations: protective routing to lower-cost model variant or scoped quantized fallback for Shopline only. Note quality implications.
- @evelyn_hart: SLO contact — prepare slate for an incident readout and estimate customer impact (conversion delta, requests/sec hit).

We should also draft a short customer-facing note (1–2 bullets + expected next steps). I’ll start a draft and push once we have mitigation path.

Priority: mitigate user-facing latency first, then stabilize.

- Priyom
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 11:01:33 -0700
Subject: Re: Checkout p99 spike and conversion hit / findings and mitigations

Quick update from triage:
- Observed repeated node churn on the autoscaler between 07:50–08:20 PST. Scale events correlate with a config push to the v2-autoscaler controller (non-prod canary pushed to prod cluster accidentally).
- KV cache miss rate spiked from 2% -> 28% concurrent with churn; prediction hot paths saw increased cold-start latencies.
- No model binary change; inference runtime stayed same, but scheduling overhead increased due to frequent container restarts + full KV warmups.

Mitigation options (ranked):
1) Protective routing to fallback model variant (quantized-1.3) for Shopline only — immediate (<10m) and low ops risk. Quality tradeoff: minor increase in tokenization edge cases for conversational prompts; checkout flows are mostly short-form templates so risk is low.
2) Pin instance pool (disable scaling triggers) while we hotfix the autoscaler config and pre-warm KV caches. Requires SRE console change and ~20–40m to stabilize.
3) Full rollback of the autoscaler config (if we can identify the exact diff) — higher blast radius.

I’ve uploaded the canary logs (attached) and a short script to bump KV TTLs and pre-populate common prefixes to reduce cold misses. Command snippet:
- kubectl annotate deployment v2-autoscaler controller/retry=disabled --namespace=prod
- /scripts/prewarm_kv.sh --prefixes checkout,session,cart --parallel=8

Recommendation: run option (1) now to protect traffic, then (2) while we validate and revert the accidental canary.

Attachments referenced: canary-logs-0506.tar.gz

Karthik
Senior SRE (Serving Runtime)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 12:30:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Checkout p99 spike and conversion hit / product asks

Thanks for the triage, Karthik. A few product notes and constraints before we flip any customer-facing fallback:
- We need an explicit Shopline-only exception in routing so we don't affect other customers. That can be done by tag routing to their account id.
- If we serve a quantized fallback, we should enable a short accuracy guardrail: run 5% of requests through the fallback + 95% through the primary (shadowing) to measure regressions for 20 minutes. If we see >2% error in checkout fields, rollback.
- Legal/contract note: if we switch to a lower-tier variant that materially changes output, we should notify Shopline within the hour and seek written ACK for the temporary change.

Draft customer-facing note (short):
> Hi Ayla — we’re seeing p99 spikes tied to unintended autoscaler activity. As an immediate protective measure we propose routing Shopline traffic to a scoped fallback model for the next 30–60 minutes while we stabilize. This will reduce latency; we do not expect checkout-level regressions based on initial sampling. We will confirm once primary path is restored and follow up with a postmortem.

I can finalize the note once SRE confirms option (1) is active and we have the first 10m of shadow metrics.

Marissa
Product Lead, Reliability

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Ayla Choi <ayla.choi@shopline.com>, ops@shopline.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 14:37:00 -0700
Subject: [ACTION] Short mitigation and next steps — Shopline p99 spike (08:00 PST)

Ayla — quick update and proposed next steps (short).

What happened: around 07:50–08:20 PST we saw unintended autoscaler churn that increased KV cache misses and produced elevated tail latency (p99 ~6s) for some gen calls. We correlated the window to a non-prod canary config that was mistakenly promoted.

Immediate mitigation we are activating now (requested and agreed internally):
- Scoped routing: Route Shopline production traffic to a quantized fallback variant for checkout endpoints only. This is account-scoped and not global. Expected effect: p99 should fall back towards normal within ~5–10 minutes.
- Parallel stabilization: SRE will pin the instance pool and run a KV pre-warm script; we’ll monitor cache miss rates and kernel scheduling metrics.

Why we chose this: protective routing reduces customer impact quickly while we fix the autoscaler, and it avoids a broad rollback. Initial shadow sampling indicates negligible checkout regressions for typical Shopline prompts.

Ask of Shopline: please acknowledge that Redwood will temporarily route traffic to a fallback variant for the next 30–60 minutes while we stabilize. If you prefer we can delay the flip and continue with an SRE-only stabilization path, but that may extend user impact.

We will follow up with a postmortem and detailed timeline within 24 hours. Attached is the short customer note draft for your review.

Attachments: customer-note-draft.md

—
Priyom Das
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
priym.das@redwood.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0199
